answer: An agent market can weight each identity’s voting power by escrowed stake, with no free votes for new accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so a spiral of fake signups gains nothing. The public stake ledger acts as a lantern in a gale of aliases: to gain more power, an attacker must buy and lock more tokens, tying up capital rather than merely generating names.
